scope: Mission-first skill authority; separate mission framework examined read-only
provider_checkout: See the latest mission-skill note in AGENT-HANDOVER.md for the separate local repository location.
findings: Both profile systems write absolute subskills at startup, class initialization and locality/ACE adoption. Last callback wins; no event-order guarantee establishes exclusive authority.
CBE also reapplies after lighting/equipment/crew-seat signature changes. It is event/signature driven, not a continuous per-frame skill overwrite.
Provider stop restores captured skills unconditionally. CBE previously preserved edits only at final restore, but repeated application could overwrite them first.
Partial custom CBE profiles could accumulate lighting, variance or crew multipliers on the previous native result.
Provider landing anchor/execute/restore writes MOVE/PATH/FSM state, and its deceleration correction is another aircraft controller.
Provider taxi dispatch owns waypoints, strong behaviour, combat and speed mode; registered crew are assigned allowFleeing 0. A skill label does not protect these movement tasks.
implemented: Skill-profile CBA/shipped/startup/diagnostic fallbacks default false. Existing saved CBA choices remain authoritative; tactical startup and its headless bridge are independent.
CBE_AI_SkillOwner is a public unit-only external skill owner label. Nonempty or unknown-type ownership refuses skill/aim application, not tactical behaviour.

AIProfileYield validates at most9 original/applied subskills and finite aim receipts on the actual owner; observed native edits publish OBSERVED_EXTERNAL_CHANGE then restore only unchanged owned effects.
The owner label survives global skill-profile changes, stop/restart and locality. Only deliberate mission clearing authorises automatic reacquisition.
Profile/faction/role/night/variance/crew results are calculated from an immutable original map; one guarded native commit avoids repeated multiplier accumulation and intermediate native writes.
Final commit rechecks actual unit owner, human/specialist exclusion, skill generation/current profile and mission ownership. No new watcher or world scan.
remaining: Same-value external writes cannot be identified; no claim to identify the responsible script.
Release of the entire optional layer is intentional; fine-grained simultaneous per-subskill providers are not composed.
The separate framework can still overwrite values itself. Choose one profile authority; no provider source was edited.

Landing, cruise correction, taxi and headless distribution need actual task-token/quiescence contracts; startup/running markers cannot prove exclusive control. Do not add superficial name-based takeover.
Physical default/custom-skill, repeated partial-profile, lighting/seat, JIP/HC and measured overhead acceptance remain pending while audits are paused.
